flawed_step: Lines 39–40 assert that a trivial path containing an added isolated vertex cannot cover n vertices and assume n > 1, but the reduction allows n = 1.
counterexample: Let H have one vertex v and no edges, so n=1. The constructed G consists of v and the 17 added isolated vertices. Since |V(G)|−17=1, the trivial path PG=(u1) is a simple path visiting exactly the required number of vertices, yet it contains an added isolated vertex. This directly contradicts lines 39–40 and invalidates the inference that every qualifying PG must use only vertices of H.
assessment_summary: The reverse-direction argument relies on an unjustified n>1 assumption. Although this boundary case can be repaired separately, the proof as written contains a false relied-upon claim.
